bounded_slice.candidate: Repository-native producer-attribution authenticity audit for the p1-sa-601 evidence package.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: First-party Git and GitHub documentation only. Tested whether immutable Git object identity plus GitHub commit-signature verification can support a narrow producer-attribution claim without richer-mode/protected/manual execution, paid or finite monthly quota, hidden external executor, or second semantic leaf.

primary_sources.observation: Git documents its object store as content-addressable: an object key is derived from the object type/size header plus content and can retrieve that exact stored object later.

primary_sources.source: GitHub Docs - About commit signature verification
primary_sources.observation: GitHub marks commits Verified when supported signatures are successfully verified, stores a persistent verification record with verified_at when verification occurs, and states that GitHub does not possess contributors' private signing keys.

primary_sources.source: GitHub Docs - Displaying verification statuses for all of your commits
primary_sources.observation: GitHub explicitly notes that Git author/committer identity fields can be set by the user; vigilant mode increases confidence but a signed committer does not guarantee a distinct author's consent.
Commit responses expose verification.verified, reason, signature, payload and verified_at, making the platform verification result replay-readable as repository-native evidence metadata.

result.repository_object_identity: pass for exact repository-object replay identity within Git's hash/object model; it does not identify a human or agent producer by itself
result.credential_possession: conditional pass when a commit signature is cryptographically verified under GitHub's supported key/account or certificate rules
result.platform_actor_attribution: conditional narrow pass only for the claim that GitHub verified the commit signature and associated verification metadata under its account/key or certificate rules; this is not equivalent to independent proof of the real-world producer
result.independent_observation_authenticity: fail/unresolved; neither Git object identity nor GitHub Verified status proves that an observation was independently sensed, that one credential maps uniquely to one producer, or that Sybil/credential-sharing/compromise is absent
result.manual_trust_ceremony: general local GPG/SSH/S-MIME producer authentication remains conditional on key/account/certificate setup or trust policy; GitHub web-signed commits avoid a user-supplied signing key but still attest a GitHub-mediated commit event rather than independently proving the underlying producer or observation
result.package_completeness: conditional pass for a narrow evidence package that states only exact object identity plus GitHub's recorded verification result; fail for any stronger producer or independent-observation authenticity claim
result.replayability: pass for replaying immutable object identity and GitHub verification fields from repository-native data, subject to repository/API availability and hash/signature assumptions
result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact audit and replay package: no hosted runner, Codespaces, external model/API, protected execution or manual user step is required to interpret already-materialized object and verification metadata. GitHub's repository service is treated only as repository transport/platform verification evidence, not as external task execution.
result.quota_zero_assessment: The narrow replay mechanism uses Git object identity and repository-native verification metadata. It requires no optional monthly/trial/paid runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package, cloud-credit or model quota; ordinary API rate limits remain an interruption risk handled by cross-invocation continuation, not a finite monthly acceptance dependency.
result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: semantic inputs were frozen sanitized controls, own scientist_agents LATEST/p1-sa-601, and first-party public Git/GitHub documentation only. No O/downstream/other-worker/shared-ledger/protected-primary/scheduler semantics were consumed.
result.uncertainty: Not proven: identity of a real human/agent behind an account or key, key custody, compromise, certificate governance, independent sensing, Sybil resistance, repository compromise, hash collision resistance beyond standard assumptions, or cross-platform equivalence.
